newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Senator says Swiss used "Jewish assets".
newsitem.headline: U.S. Senator says Swiss used "Jewish assets".

text.p: Charging that Switzerland "blatantly benefitted from the Holocaust," the head of the Senate Banking Committee on Wednesday said the Swiss government forged secret deals to use Jewish assets to compensate its own citizens.

New York Republican Sen. Alfonse D'Amato made his comments at an emotionally charged hearing in which Holocaust survivors wept in recalling how Swiss banks refused to help them track family bank accounts -- demanding that they produce death certificates for people who perished in Nazi death camps.

D'Amato, whose committee has been probing the Swiss financial role in the Second World War, said newly discovered documents showed the Swiss were bigger collaborators with the Nazis than previously imagined.

He accused Switzerland of stalling justice by setting up a commission that will take five years to report its findings on the amount of looted assets deposited by Germans in their Swiss safe haven. He said that by the time the commission made its report, many heirs will have died.

The senator said researchers had uncovered documents showing that the Swiss, in a secret 1949 deal with Poland, used assets of Polish Jews to compensate Swiss citizens for the nationalisation of their property in the then-Communist country. He said that similar deals were struck later with Hungary and Czechoslovakia.

He said the Swiss were able to do this by confiscating the heirless property of Polish Jews in Switzerland "for the benefit of Swiss citizens to satisfy the claims of those Swiss whose property was nationalised by the Polish Communist government."
D'Amato added, "I am very concerned that Swiss citizens and corporations blatantly benefited from the Holocaust while the interests of the survivors were totally ignored."

"Clearly, Switzerland has many questions to answer. Most importantly I want to know where all the hundreds of millions of dollars of assets that Nazi Germany deposited in Swiss banks went. It is clear from the information that we have seen that a great amount of these assets were looted from victims of the Holocaust. I want to know where this money is and who has it," he said.

D'Amato said other newly discovered documents showed that the Germans, during the war, invested between $414 million and $816 million in Swiss enterprises and sold the Swiss hundreds of millions of dollars in looted gold.
But after the war, Switzerland admitted to having only $250 million in German assets and kept half for itself while compensating the allies with $125 million.
D'Amato said that the Swiss also shortchanged the allies on the looted gold -- giving them only $60 million of what was really worth about $625 million.
Nobel Peace Prize winner Elie Wiesel, a survivor of two Nazi death camps, told the hearing Switzerland had much to answer for because of its conduct in the war.

"Switzerland did save some Jewish lives but how is one to explain that the very idea of stamping German passports with a 'J' for Jewish came not from Germany but from Switzerland? How is one to explain that Switzerland collaboated with German agents to keep Jewish money in their safes? Why did it take so long for this to come out?" he asked.
